objective: Give an explicit fixed-quotient lifting theorem with exposed constants, an exact scaling obstruction to a shortcut, and sharper residual recycling for the C15 nonsplit family.

atomic_claims.text: A k-clique quotient motif lifts to q-vertex groups at cost at most (q+L_k-1)^2 using a modulus congruent to one modulo L_k=lcm(1,...,k-2), with L_2=1.
A quotient partition into h cliques gives cp<=h*q^2+2q*sum ell_j+sum ell_j^2+P, exposing all template-dependent terms.
The four-vertex star satisfies cp=B(4), but its quotient-only lift costs 3q^2 while its actual split expansion has cp=(5q^2+q)/2; quotient linear errors cannot be silently scaled as linear errors.
The unedited nonsplit chordal family G_q from C15 has cp<=4q^2+2q+6<=B(8q), by merging its actual residual into five cliques.

assumptions: Finite simple graphs and exact edge partitions.
A specified quotient clique partition and supplied within-group partitions.
The quotient and its partition are fixed for the uniform-in-q consequence.
C01 and C15 written construction inputs.
risks: No mathematical execution, optimality proof or verifier receipt.
The padding constant depends on motif sizes; a fixed-template theorem does not prove a uniform all-chordal result.
Edgeless block replacement need not preserve chordality; K2 to K(q,q) is an explicit guard.
The sharper large-residual-clique construction cannot inherit C15's small-piece edge-edit bound without new analysis.
